questions.q: In ancient Greece, the wrestling school was called:
questions.qPa: ਪ੍ਰਾਚੀਨ ਯੂਨਾਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੁਸ਼ਤੀ ਦੇ ਸਕੂਲ ਨੂੰ ਕੀ ਕਿਹਾ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਸੀ?
questions.explanation: Palaestra was the physical training area, specifically for wrestling.

questions.q: What was the primary aim of physical education in ancient Sparta?
questions.explanation: Sparta's entire societal structure was focused on creating fierce warriors.

questions.q: A physical education teacher in ancient Greece was known as a:
questions.explanation: Paidotribe translates roughly to 'boy rubber' or trainer.

questions.q: Which educational philosophy emphasizes 'learning by doing' and practical experience?
questions.qPa: ਕਿਹੜਾ ਵਿਦਿਅਕ ਫਲਸਫਾ 'ਕਰ ਕੇ ਸਿੱਖਣ' ਅਤੇ ਵਿਹਾਰਕ ਅਨੁਭਵ 'ਤੇ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ?
questions.explanation: Pragmatism, associated heavily with John Dewey, centers on experiential learning.

questions.q: Rousseau is considered the father of which philosophy?
questions.explanation: Jean-Jacques Rousseau championed Naturalism, advocating that education should follow the natural development of the child.

questions.q: Which city-state focused on the harmonious development of both mind and body?
questions.explanation: Athens sought to create well-rounded citizens, balancing intellectual and physical pursuits.

questions.q: Which philosophy holds that winning is secondary to character building and sportsmanship?
questions.explanation: Idealism focuses on mind, values, and character development above material outcomes like winning.

questions.q: The Spartan education system for boys was called:
questions.explanation: The Agoge was the rigorous education and training program mandated for all male Spartan citizens.
